method: Independent direct HTTP status, redirect, media-type, byte-length and content-hash checks; page-level PDF extraction for the 2023 equity financing; direct company, manager, sponsor and policy-lender review for business model, project boundary, Temasek financing, later rounds, project ownership and exit search

verifiedClaims: Eavor expressly describes a capital-light technology licensing and services model
Eavor expects only selective project equity and accepts reduced control
Geretsried is a first-of-a-kind commercial project with four operating lateral pairs and about 8.5 MWth in May 2026
Eavor announced first electricity production at Geretsried on December 5, 2025
The release describes Eavor as a Calgary-based technology-oriented energy company
Eavor completed a US$40 million corporate financing on February 16, 2021
Temasek participated alongside venture, strategic and corporate investors
Proceeds supported technology commercialization, pipeline scaling and research and development
Temasek described Eavor as a Canada-based company developing proprietary geothermal technology
Temasek placed Eavor among industrials and energy investments rather than identifying an infrastructure fund or mandate
Eavor completed a $182 million equity round on October 25, 2023
Temasek and other existing investors contributed to the round
The release emphasizes technology development and deployment, not a disclosed Temasek project-SPV interest
Canada Growth Fund committed up to approximately C$138 million on June 3, 2025
The financing followed CGF's C$90 million preferred-equity investment in 2023
The release calls Eavor an advanced geothermal technology company based in Calgary and does not disclose a Temasek follow-on
Geretsried sits in Eavor Erdwärme Geretsried GmbH & Co. KG
Sponsor interests are approximately 40% Chubu, 15% bp, 15% OMV and 30% Eavor/Enex combined
The project is designed for about 8.2 MW electric and 64 MW thermal output
JBIC and co-lenders provided about EUR131 million of project financing
The Geretsried SPV will build, own and operate the geothermal power and district-heat plant
The policy lender treats Geretsried as a project-level infrastructure investment

exitSearch.result: No direct Temasek sale, transfer or exit was found. Eavor's public materials confirm a 2023 Temasek follow-on but do not provide a current cap table, while the 2025 CGF financing does not name a Temasek follow-on. Temasek's cutoff ownership therefore remains unresolved, but the direct-infrastructure scope failure does not depend on that status.

responseSourceHealthCorrections: The initial response's December 4, 2025 commissioning date was corrected in the sole repair to the December 5 date stated by Eavor's direct release.
The 2023 release describes a $182 million financing but does not label the total's currency in the extracted text; the decision preserves the financing event without relying on a currency assumption.
Chubu discloses only an approximately 30% combined Eavor/Enex project interest, so no standalone Eavor percentage or control is inferred.
The existence of one co-owned operating project does not override Eavor's own capital-light licensing and services model.
No Temasek infrastructure fund, mandate, security, vehicle, governance right or current percentage was publicly disclosed.
